docs.title: MSF React Template
docs.text: This repository provides a scaffold for spinning up a new React-based application using the MSF conventions. It is intended to reduce setup friction while keeping the generated app aligned with the broader MSF standard tooling and structure.

docs.title: Project purpose
docs.text:
The package is designed to provide:

  • a CLI-based app generator
  • a templated starter app structure
  • consistent file organization for new frontend projects
  • reduced setup work for teams creating new MSF applications

docs.title: Repository shape
docs.text:
react-template/
├── bin/
├── template/
├── README.md
├── package.json
├── mkdocs.yml
├── .github/
└── openwiki/

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
npm create @msflib/react-template my-app

or, depending on the package distribution, the CLI entry may be invoked through the package bin configuration.

docs.title: Operational guidance
docs.text:
• keep the generated structure predictable and minimal
  • document any required framework assumptions clearly
  • preserve the package's role as a scaffold rather than a full app
  • keep the template aligned with the rest of the MSF frontend repos

docs.title: Project overview
docs.text: The @msflib/react-template package is the templating layer for new MSF-based React applications. It acts as a generator rather than a full application, which means its documentation should center on installability, scaffold structure, and expected downstream usage.

docs.title: Main responsibilities
docs.text:
This package is intended to provide:

  • a bootstrap command for creating new apps
  • starter layout files under template/
  • command-line installation and setup helpers
  • a consistent starting point for MSF frontend projects

docs.title: Key package conventions
docs.text:
"bin": {
  "create-msf-app": "bin/index.js"
},
"files": [
  "bin",
  "template"
]

This packaging keeps the utility focused on the generator and its generated output.

docs.title: Development guidance
docs.text:
• keep the generated app structure clear and low-friction
  • avoid adding project-specific assumptions to the template
  • document any new generator flags or file conventions clearly
  • validate the scaffold against a real generated app before publishing
